q: What does the CAPITAL syllable in the pronunciation line show?
o: The first syllable of the word
The stressed syllable, said louder and longer
A letter you do not say
why: Stress is not written in Tagalog spelling, so the line shows it in CAPITALS.

q: How is the little word ng in Kumain ako ng mangga said?
o: Like the letters N and G
Like the ing in sing, with no vowel
why: On its own, the word ng is always said nang.

q: Why is it malaking bahay and not malaki bahay?
o: malaking is the plural of malaki
Tagalog joins a describing word to its noun with the linker -ng
bahay always needs ng before it
malaki bahay means a small house
why: malaki ends in a vowel, so the linker -ng joins it to bahay.

q: Why does every greeting begin with Magandang?
o: maganda (beautiful) is joined to the time of day with the linker -ng
It is the polite form of maganda
why: Tagalog says beautiful morning: maganda + the linker -ng + umaga.

q: Your friend's grandmother asks you a question. How do you say yes?
why: opo is the polite yes; oo is for friends.

q: Which is the polite How are you? for an older stranger?
why: To an elder, use the polite kayo with po: Kumusta po kayo?

q: Which word goes before a person's name in Ako si Ana?
why: si goes before a person's name: Ako si Ana.

q: You tell a Filipino friend about you and your sister: We're teachers. Which we?
why: kami leaves the listener out; tayo would include your friend.

q: Why is Ka si Mark wrong?
o: ka cannot start a sentence; use ikaw there
why: ka comes right after the first word; at the start, use ikaw.

q: How do you say I'm from Cebu?
why: taga- + place means from that place: Taga-Cebu ako.

q: Why is it Ilang taon, not Ilan taon?
o: ilan ends in n, so the linker -g joins it to taon
why: After n the linker is just -g: ilang taon.

q: A friend asks Paano ka? What did they mean to say?
o: Nothing: How are you? is Kumusta ka?
why: Paano ka? is a word-for-word copy of English; How are you? is Kumusta ka?

q: The vendor is holding a bag in her hand. You ask how much it is. Which word?
why: iyan is that, near the listener.

q: How do you say This is Ana?
why: si goes before a person's name: Ito si Ana.

q: Your friend points at a bag. How do you say It's expensive? (mahal = expensive)
why: siya is for people; for things Tagalog uses ito, iyan or iyon.

q: Which marker goes before a name when the person is the topic?
why: si marks a name as the topic; ang is for ordinary nouns.

q: How do you say the teacher's house?
why: guro is an ordinary noun, so the owner takes ng: bahay ng guro.

q: Why is kay Maynila wrong?
o: kay is for people; a place takes sa
kay is only for the topic
kay must come after the place
why: kay is for people; places take sa: sa Maynila.

q: Which linker joins mabait (kind) to bata (child)?
why: mabait ends in a consonant, so the linker is na.

q: Which phrase means the same as magandang bahay?
why: Both orders are correct; the linker sits between the words: bahay na maganda.

q: Why is it pagkaing masarap, with a g?
o: pagkain ends in n, so the linker is just -g
why: After n, the linker is -g: pagkaing masarap.

q: How do you say my name?
why: The ng form ko goes after the noun: pangalan ko.

q: Why is Gusto ako ng kape wrong?
o: gusto takes the ng form: Gusto ko
gusto is only for things you like, not want
why: After gusto, use the ng form ko: Gusto ko ng kape.

q: Which means our house, talking about your own family to a friend?
why: namin is our without the listener; natin includes them.

q: Where does ba go in a yes-or-no question?
o: After the first word, and after ka if ka is there
why: ba goes right after the first word and after ka: Pagod ka ba?

q: Which word asks where something is right now, as in Where's the restroom?
why: nasaan asks where a thing or person is: Nasaan ang CR?

q: How do you ask Is she tired?
why: siya comes after ba: Pagod ba siya?

q: Your friend asks May kape ba? (Is there coffee?) and there is none. What do you answer?
why: wala answers "Is there any…?" when there is none; hindi is just "not".

q: How do you tell a friend "Don't leave"?
why: huwag is the word for "don't", and the linker joins it to ka: huwag kang.

q: Lola asks Pagod ka na ba? (Are you tired?) and you are not. What do you say?
why: It is a plain "no", so hindi; Lola gets po.

q: Why is it apat na aso but limang aso?
o: na is for animals, -ng for people
Both are correct for either number
apat ends in a consonant, so the linker is na; lima ends in a vowel, so it takes -ng
-ng is only used with Spanish numbers
why: The linker depends on the sound before it: na after a consonant, -ng after a vowel.

q: Which means "three hours"?
why: Durations use native numbers with the linker; alas-tres is three o'clock.

q: A vendor says Singkwenta po. How much is it?
why: singkwenta is the Spanish 50, the usual way to say small prices.

q: Which sentence means "I have a car"?
why: may goes straight before the noun, and the owner comes after it: May kotse ako.

q: Your friend asks May pera ka ba? (Do you have money?) You have none. What do you answer?
why: The opposite of may is wala: there's none.

q: Why is it Mayroon akong aso and not Mayroon ako aso?
o: After mayroon, the pronoun takes the linker -ng
ako is wrong after mayroon; use ko
why: mayroon is followed by the pronoun plus the linker: akong.

q: How do you make clear that your kapatid is a brother?
why: kapatid has no sex; add lalaki with the linker na.

q: Who can you call Tita?
o: Your aunts, and also your parents' friends
why: tito and tita are used for parents' friends too, not only for real uncles and aunts.

q: "My dad is a doctor" =
why: The job comes first, then ang tatay ko, with the ng pronoun ko for "my".

q: Which means "for her"?
why: After para sa, use the sa form: kaniya (often written kanya).

q: How do you ask where Ana is right now?
why: nasaan asks where someone or something is; nasa is the answer word.

q: "This is for Juan." Which word goes before Juan?
why: With a person's name, use kay: para kay Juan.

q: "Are you tired?" (to a friend) =
why: The predicate pagod comes first, then ka, then ba.

q: What does Ako ay guro. mean?
o: I am a teacher. (topic first, a bit formal)
why: ay puts the topic first; it means the same as Guro ako.

q: Kumain __ __ kayo? (Have you eaten? polite) Which words fill the gaps, in order?
why: na comes before po, and the longer pronoun kayo comes last.

q: Where does -um- go in kain?
why: -um- goes right before the first vowel of the root.

q: Why is it Kumain ako and not Kumain ko?
o: ko is only used in questions
With an -um- verb the doer takes the ang form
ako shows that it happened in the past
why: Actor focus: the doer is the topic, so it takes the ang form ako.

q: In "Juan drank water", which word goes before tubig (water)?
why: The doer already has the ang form; the thing takes ng.

q: How do you turn magluto into "cooked"?
o: Add na after it: magluto na
Change the m to n: nagluto
why: nag- instead of mag- shows the action is finished.

q: Why does nag-aral have a hyphen?
o: It marks the catch before aral
It shows the action is finished
why: The hyphen stands for the catch before a root that starts with a vowel.

q: In Nagluto si Ana ng pancit (Ana cooked pancit), which noun is the topic?
why: A mag- verb is actor focus: the doer, si Ana, is the topic.

q: How do you make the future of kain?
why: The future repeats the first syllable and has no -um-: kakain.

q: Which sentence is wrong?
why: bukas (tomorrow) needs the future form: Kakain ako bukas.

q: What does Nagtatrabaho ako sa ospital. mean?
o: I worked at a hospital once.
I will work at a hospital.
I want to work at a hospital.
why: The ongoing form is used for a regular job or habit.

q: Which word for "I" goes after gusto?
why: gusto takes the ng form: Gusto ko.

q: How do you join gusto ko to a verb?
o: Add the linker: Gusto kong kumain
Put ng between them: Gusto ko ng kumain
Use ay: Gusto ko ay kumain
why: A verb after gusto ko is joined with the linker -ng: Gusto kong kumain.

q: "I can speak Tagalog" (I know how) is…
why: marunong is "know how to"; puwede is "may, allowed".

q: In Kinain ko ang mangga, which noun is the topic?
why: With an -in verb the thing takes ang: ang mangga is the topic.

q: Which verb fits "Juan cooked the adobo"?
why: "the adobo" is a particular thing, so object focus: Niluto ni Juan ang adobo.

q: In object focus, the doer takes…
why: The doer of an -in verb takes the ng form: ko, mo, niya, ni Ana.

q: What is ulam?
o: The dish you eat with rice
why: A meal is kanin plus ulam, the dish that goes with the rice.

q: How do you order one adobo from the staff?
why: Number + linker + dish, and po to the staff: Isang adobo po.

q: "Kumain ka na?" is usually…
o: A way to ask for the bill
An order to eat right now
why: Filipinos ask "Have you eaten?" the way English speakers ask "How are you?"

q: Which means "three o'clock"?
why: The clock uses alas- + a Spanish number: alas-tres.

q: What does mamaya mean?
why: mamaya is later today; "maybe" is baka or siguro.

q: Which means "five minutes"?
why: Lengths of time use native numbers with the linker: limang minuto.

q: Which word means "left"?
why: kaliwa is left; kanan is right.

q: What do you say to get off a jeepney?
why: Para po! asks the driver to stop.

q: "to Makati" is…
why: Places take sa; kay is for people.

q: What does paki- add to a verb?
why: paki- turns a verb into a polite request: pakiabot, please pass.

q: "Don't leave!" (to a friend) is…
why: "Don't" is huwag, and the pronoun after it takes the linker: kang.

q: Which is a polite command to an older person?
why: Use po kayo with anyone who gets po.

q: "not yet" is…
why: pa is still or yet: Hindi pa is not yet.

q: Where do the little words go?
o: At the end of the sentence
why: Little words sit right after the first word.

q: Which order is right?
why: One-syllable ka first, then na, then ba.

q: "cheaper" is…
why: mas means more: mas mura.

q: After kaysa, a person's name takes…
why: kay is for people after kaysa: kaysa kay Ana.

q: "the cheapest" is…
why: pinaka- means most: pinakamura.

q: Is "Nag-shopping kami" bad Tagalog?
o: No, it is normal everyday Taglish
why: Mixing English words into Tagalog grammar is normal in Manila.

q: What would you say to your grandmother?
why: With elders, use the careful form with po.

q: "Tara!" means…
why: Tara! is a casual "Let's go!"
